headline: Pretrained genomic models are being applied to phage-host and prophage prediction
label: Viral Genome Language Models
summary: Recent preprints test whether DNA foundation models and phylogenetic embeddings transfer to phage, prophage, and microbiome prediction tasks.
synthesis: The common thread is adapting pretrained genomic sequence representations to viral and bacterial host-associated prediction. FoundedPBI ensembles three DNA foundation models with long-context aggregation to predict phage-bacterium interactions from whole genomes, reporting F1 gains. LAMBDA takes a complementary route, providing a benchmark for genomic language model embeddings on phage-bacteria discrimination across probing, fine-tuning, and diagnostic evaluations. Micro16S extends the representation question to 16S rRNA, learning continuous phylogenetic embeddings from GTDB-based triplet and pair losses for microbiome deep learning. What is new here is the explicit evaluation of foundation-model embeddings alongside task-specific predictors. All three are preprints, so the reported gains and benchmark conclusions require independent validation.
